title: The arithmetic category and stable recovery of lattice factors
main_claim: For Γ in the class K (ICC groups commensurable with lattices in finite products of property-(T) simple groups over local fields), and arbitrary 2-cocycles: (Thm 1.1) L_ω(Λ)^t ≅ L_ν(Π)^s iff t=s and Λ≅Π with cohomologous pulled-back cocycles, with every specified isomorphism being canonical up to inner conjugation (so the fundamental group is trivial); (Thm 1.2) every bifinite neighbour P of L_μ(Γ) is L_ω(Λ)^t, with Λ commensurable to Γ and a finite-type cocycle ratio; (Thm 1.3) a complete Hom/summand/fusion calculus of bifinite correspondences in terms of full-germ stabilizers and projective fibre representations. Exhaustion (Thm 1.3(i)) is imported from the companion's Theorem 1.2.

issues.location: Prop. 2.1 (Arithmetic exhaustion) / Thm 1.3(i); used in Lemma 4.2, proof of Thm 1.1, Cor. 5.x
issues.description: All of the paper's geometric content comes from one external result, companion Theorem 1.2. That is where every model is shown to exhaust all bifinite correspondences. This paper only proves the algebraic calculus on top of it, and every main theorem fails without it. Taken together, the consequences are very strong: trivial fundamental group and stable Connes rigidity for L(SL_3(Z)) and all of K, integrality of the index of every finite-index subfactor of these factors, and Out(L(Γ)) = Hom(Γ,T)⋊Out(Γ). So the companion needs a full audit. This is a dependency note, not a gap in this paper.
issues.evidence: Sec. 2: 'We use exactly the following theorem ... This is the Arithmetic exhaustion theorem of the complete companion [Theorem 1.2]'. End of Sec. 3: 'We now apply the geometric input...establishes every assertion of Theorem 1.3'. The sibling review of the companion on the hive board covered only about 40%.

coverage:
Read the whole paper (about 2,150 lines of LaTeX in sections 1–5); the companion paper was not read. Steps checked:
(1) Lemma 3.1: the full stabilizer of a germ is a graph of finite-index subgroups, and {d} is the only finite C_d-orbit; the ICC centralizer argument is correct.
(2) Exact projective induction and the graph-bundle unitary, including the phase computation ω(δb,δa)β(b,a)=μ(b,a).
(3) Hom theorem 3.4: the bound on Hilbert–Schmidt column sums plus constancy along C_x-orbits forces maps to be diagonal in germ labels. Integer dimensions of the actual summands follow.
(4) Double-coset fusion formula, the q_m coboundary, and the index-counting identities.
(5) Lemma 4.1 (extension), Lemma 4.2 (intrinsic grading and its finite-span test), and Lemma 4.3 (Pimsner–Popa boundedness via E_M(ξ*ξ)=‖ξ‖²).
(6) Lemma 4.4 (minimal corner gives L_ω(Λ)) and Prop. 4.5: the s_a/q_a/t_a construction, the ratio identity δ*ω=(∂λ)μ\bar κ (verified by hand), [Λ:B]<∞ via commensuration, and Λ being ICC.
(7) Proof of Thm 1.1: dimensions t/s and s/t forced to equal 1, one orbit with a 1-dimensional fibre, the cochain equation, and implementation of θ by z and w.
(8) Section 5: the commensurability corollary, Out(L(Γ)) injectivity, reduced C*-algebra recovery, the SL_3(Z) covolume lemma, and the endomorphism corollary (right dimension 1 forces A_d=Γ).
sibling_notes: Sibling rank3 (Arithmeticity-of-twisted-finite-correspondences..., probably the companion that supplies Thm 1.2 exhaustion) reported no_gap_found but only about 40% coverage. It flagged that the claims are huge (trivial fundamental group, stable Connes rigidity). This paper inherits those claims entirely through that one theorem. Its own algebraic layer is sound, so remaining risk sits in the unread parts of the companion (its Sec 4, 5 and most of 6–8).
